events.title: Berry Hollow abrasion at Wildcat Ridge
events.summary: Perseverance abraded a circular patch, named Berry Hollow, in the Wildcat Ridge rock on sol 504 to investigate its composition; PIXL scanned it on sols 505 (BH1) and 507 (BH2). NASA gives the abrasion patch as about 5 cm (2 in) across.
events.found: PIXL identified calcium sulfate in the Berry Hollow vein: anhydrite with gypsum and bassanite. For the BH2 scan the study reports about 45% anhydrite, 37% gypsum and 18% bassanite among those phases. These values describe the centimetre-scale patch only.
events.scientificValue: NASA describes the delta as one of the best places on Mars to search for potential signs of ancient microbial life; sulfates like these precipitate from water and record how water moved through the delta sediments.

coordinateSource.title: NASA Perseverance rover waypoints (MMGIS)
coordinateSource.note: Rover position at waypoint 26_1222 (sol 502); raw images from sol 504 are tagged site 26 drive 1222, so the rover had not moved. The patch is within arm's reach of this point; its exact offset is not published.

events.title: Three Forks sample depot
events.summary: Perseverance dropped 10 sample tubes in a zigzag pattern, each about 5 to 15 m apart, on flat ground near the base of the delta at 'Three Forks'. events.title: Perseverance backshell and parachute imaged by Ingenuity
events.summary: Ingenuity photographed Perseverance's backshell, supersonic parachute and debris from 8 m altitude during Flight 26 on April 19, 2022. The parachute and backshell were jettisoned at about 2.1 km altitude during landing and hit the ground at about 126 km/h.
events.found: NASA: the backshell sits upright; its protective coating appears intact, many of the 80 suspension lines are visible and appear intact, and the parachute canopy shows no signs of damage from supersonic inflation.
events.scientificValue: Engineers for Mars Sample Return requested the images because they may show how the landing components performed.
